title: surgical-model-flipbook-scratchpad-rz
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes for a surgical model flip we need to run for the hosted API + Dedicated customers this week. Goal: flip traffic from model@v3-alpha -> model@v3-stable for text-generation while keeping latency and hallucination regressions within tight bounds. This is a scratchpad — not-yet-reviewed by PS or SRE.

High-level plan:
- Preflight (T-48h): smoke + perf tests green on a dedicated staging pool.
- Warmup (T-24h to T-2h): synthetic warmup traffic, KV cache priming for top-100 prefixes, seed client cohorts.
- Micro-canary (T0): 1% traffic to 10 clients (cohort ids listed below) for 30m.
- Ramp phases: 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% (hold windows & watch thresholds).
- Rollback/Pin: immediate pin to model@v3-alpha if any threshold breached.

Cohort selection (micro-canary):
- 10 low-sensitivity clients (beta partners & internal builds). NOTE: exclude mobile-apps with older SDKs that don't support streaming toggles.
- Cohort ids: beta-001..beta-010 (ask SRE to map to client tokens)

Metrics to watch (primary):
- p95 latency (generation endpoint): threshold <= 1.4x baseline
- 5xx error rate: threshold <= 0.5% absolute increase
- Mean output-quality regression: flagged by eval-set A (prompt-set A/B) -> automatic regression alert if BLEU/ROUGE/QA-drop > 3 points
- Customer-impact signal: 1+ key partner complaint = immediate pause

Secondary signals:
- GPU memory paging events (SRE alerts)
- Tail latency spikes correlated with sequence length > 1024
- Token cost delta per million tokens (should not exceed +12%)

Rollout thresholds & automated actions:
- If p95 > 1.4x baseline for 2 consecutive hold windows -> pause and pin to previous version (model@v3-alpha).
- If 5xx rate increases by >=0.5% absolute within a 15m sliding window -> rollback immediate.
- If eval-set quality drop observed -> auto-trigger canary rollback and notify product.
- For partial service errors (decoder OOMs) -> route traffic to quantized fallback (model@v3-stable-q8) and escalate.

Pins & SDK snippets (for ops runbook):
- Pin via console/API: POST /v1/routes/{route}/pin -> {"model": "model@v3-alpha"}
- Example SDK flip (Node):
  const res = await Redwood.routes.update("/api/gen", { model: "model@v3-stable", rollout: { type: "gradual", start_percent: 1 } });
  // TODO: confirm exact SDK method name before run

Warmup details (practical steps):
- KV cache priming: replay top-100 prefixes (from telemetry) against the new model variant at ~2x expected QPS for 10 minutes to seed attention caches.
- Batch-queue warmup: run 1k small requests (avg len 80 tokens) and 1k long requests (avg 600 tokens) to exercise scheduling heuristics.
- Canary clients should run a daily background warmup script for 12h prior to T0 to populate local caches (mobile-local cache).

Preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-2h):
- [ ] Perf bench: throughput and latency on dedicated staging GPUs (report attached to PR).
- [ ] E2E smoke: top-50 customer flow tests pass (auth, attachments, downstream webhooks).
- [ ] Memory & OOM stress: run mem-probe & watch for allocator growth > 20%
- [ ] Rollback runbook doc approved by PS and SRE
- [ ] Alert hooks: instrumentation dashboards prewired (p95, 5xx, regen-quality)
- [ ] Client SDK bump: verify clients in cohort support new streaming schema

Rollback playbook (short):
1) Pin route via API to model@v3-alpha (ops token).
2) Disable rollout job and reassign traffic routing rules.
3) Run a short warmup on the alpha model to avoid cold-start latency for pinned users.
4) Postmortem: collect traces, error logs, eval diffs; assign to infra or model team.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (my notes):
- Does Dedicated routing honor per-customer pinning immediately or require pool drain? (ask platform-eng)
- Can we enable TTL-less KV caching for the warmup window? SRE said TTLs are global. Possible risk of cache poisoning.
- Confirm telemetry tag to use for 'canary cohort' across logs/traces (so we can filter easily) -> should be canary_cohort=rz-surgical?
- Who will be the primary on-call? Suggest Marcos for T0 and Anya for T+1 hours.

Edge cases to think about:
- If client hits higher tail latency but only for sequences > 2048 tokens we may still progress for short-sequence users with a scoped pin. Need per-route/per-client granularity.
- If quantized fallback reduces quality for some prompts significantly, prepare a targeted prompt suppression list to route to stable path.

Smoke commands I used locally (examples):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"model":"model@v3-stable","input":"Summarize: ..."}'
- curl -X POST https://console.redwood.example/api/routes/rollout -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/api/gen","percent":1}'

Notes to self (short):
- Keep the first hold window long enough (30m) to catch slow drift in p95, but not so long that customer visibility lags. 30m seems OK.
- Use a pair of lightweight eval prompts that exercise hallucination & extraction (QA-check + numerical correctness).
- Remind product to expect slight metric wobble when KV caches are primed; note that caches may make stable appear better -> compare against uncached baseline too.

Post-rollout follow-ups (if flip completes):
- Schedule a 48h check-in with infra and SRE (collect traces + cost delta).
- Add a small experiment: A/B prompt engineering for 5% of traffic to measure quality delta for long tail prompts.

End of scratchpad — will formalize to runbook if plan looks good.

(Sign-off): Riley — will ping channel #deploys 1h before T-0 and attach the preflight checklist.
